Why Bryan businesses miss calls

Bryan sits right next to College Station but has its own character, with a historic downtown, the county courthouse and a stronger trades base. Construction employs nearly 11% of workers, and education and health care almost 30%. Texas A&M demand spills over into rentals, repairs and restaurants. Owners here often serve both cities and may be out on a job when the phone rings.

Which Bryan businesses benefit most?

  • HVAC and contractors: Catch calls from both Bryan and College Station.
  • Law firms: Near the courthouse, new clients can reach intake any time.
  • Restaurants: Downtown spots can answer table questions during the rush.

Can you keep your Bryan phone number?

Yes. Bryan callers will usually see the 979 area codes, and you can keep the number customers already know. Forward it to the AI for all calls, only after hours, or only when your team does not pick up. We can also set up a new local number. Everything is set up remotely, so you do not need new equipment or a visit to an office.

What to check before you go live

  1. Test real calls: ask awkward questions, not only easy ones, and listen to how it handles them.
  2. Set the rules: decide which calls transfer to a person and which become messages.
  3. Plan your minutes: estimate your busiest month, not an average one.
  4. Tell callers what you need to: Texas is generally treated as a one-party consent state for recording calls, but rules differ for callers in other states, so check with your advisor if you record calls.
